note: Sentinel values. Nobody who wrote this file could build the image -- the environment's egress policy blocks the registries the build needs -- so no number is guessed here. decision/0087 was written against exactly that failure mode: a budget that is a guess dressed as a requirement. The first CI run of .github/scripts/image-size.sh against a real build prints the two numbers; copy them in by hand with the SHA of the commit they were measured at. While measuredAtCommit reads UNMEASURED the gate is inactive.
toleranceNote: tolerancePercent is the measurement's noise floor, not slack. The Dockerfile pins serversideup/php:8.5-frankenphp-bookworm and node:26-bookworm-slim by TAG rather than by digest and installs apt packages unpinned, so two builds of the SAME commit on different days differ by amounts this repository did not cause. A byte-exact ratchet would go red on somebody else's upstream rebuild, and a gate that fires when nothing here changed trains people to re-run it instead of reading it -- which is how a real growth gets waved through later. Pinning the bases by digest would remove the need for this and is a larger change than item/image-size.
